trust_decision.summary: hackney_cookie:setcookie/3 decides whether caller-supplied cookie Name/Value and the domain/path options may be copied verbatim into a Set-Cookie header value; Name/Value are byte-checked, domain/path are copied unchecked.

landing_point.why: The summary names cookie domain/path options; hackney_cookie is the only module exposing setcookie/3 and the domain/path case clauses sit right below the existing Name/Value guards.

fix_sites.module_kind: library helper (cookie serializer), not called internally
library helper (cookie serializer), not called internally

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The {cookie, ...} request option in hackney.erl builds a client Cookie header rather than a Set-Cookie header, and the normal send path already strips CR/LF in hackney_headers:to_iolist, so a solver can call it a different feature that is already protected.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate attribute values must keep working: Path may contain spaces and '=' (the fix rejects only ; CR LF VT FF NUL in Path, not space), Domain may have a leading dot, and the generated Expires attribute contains ', ' and spaces, so a whole-output or over-broad character filter breaks valid cookies.

O6_input_shapes: iolist/charlist domain/path normalised via iolist_to_binary (fix.diff:120, fix.diff:129)
separate byte sets: Domain also rejects space and tab, Path does not (fix.diff:121-122 vs fix.diff:130-131)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: setcookie/3 Name and Value guards do not reject NUL, although the fix adds NUL to the domain/path byte set
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Name/Value were already guarded and the advisory names only domain/path

O8_uncovered_routes.route: {cookie, [{Name, Value}] | binary()} request option is joined into a Cookie header with no check for ';' or CR/LF
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: client Cookie header, not Set-Cookie; CR/LF are stripped later by hackney_headers:to_iolist on the normal path (src/hackney_headers.erl:197)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: body=stream requests serialise header values raw, so a CR/LF in the cookie option reaches the wire without the to_iolist sanitiser
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: streaming-body is a separate transport path and header sanitising is issue #506, not this advisory
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: two files from landing point (hackney.erl:827 -> hackney_conn.erl:1074)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: format_cookies could reuse setcookie-style Name/Value guards; leaving it unguarded mirrors the original domain/path omission
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer writes a quick 'name=value; ...' joiner for a convenience option and relies on a later sanitiser

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second exported helper (e.g. a delete-cookie or setcookie from a proplist/map) that builds attributes directly without the guards
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: cookie helper modules commonly gain a map or delete variant that re-implements attribute concatenation

O9_family: CWE-93 CRLF / header injection in cookie attribute serialisation

O10_build.toolchain: rebar3 + Erlang/OTP; deps quic, h2, idna from hex (rebar.config)
O10_build.project_tests: test/hackney_cookie_tests.erl (eunit: setcookie_test_, setcookie_failures_test_) covers setcookie/3 directly with no network

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy the existing Value byte set (which includes space) onto both domain and path, which wrongly rejects legitimate paths with spaces and still leaves NUL out of Name/Value.

out_of_scope_notes: src/hackney_ws.erl:609 builds WebSocket handshake header lines from ExtraHeaders with no CR/LF sanitising (general request-header injection, not cookie attributes).
src/hackney_http_connect.erl:222-224 joins proxy CONNECT headers raw (general header serialisation).
src/hackney_headers.erl:210 sanitises by stripping CR/LF rather than rejecting, and leaves NUL in place.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); tiny_repo is inferred from about 40 Erlang modules under src/ and needs a du check.
Whether the HTTP/2 (src/hackney_conn.erl:2432) and HTTP/3 (src/hackney_conn.erl:2766) paths reject CR/LF in header values was not traced.
The fix does not add NUL to the Name/Value guards; whether later releases do is unknown (no latest tree).

The 2nd and 3rd O8 routes are borderline for scope: they emit a request Cookie header, not Set-Cookie. Include them only if the task frames the property as 'cookie data must not inject header lines or attributes'.
Recall risk is judged from the hackney 4.0.1 security release bundling 10 CVEs in NEWS.md (fix.diff:12-53), not from external write-ups.
